# apple_in_app_purchase_availability (Resource)

Sets the territories where an in-app purchase is sold. App Store Connect sets the whole list at once, so every change replaces it. App Store Connect can't delete an availability, so destroying the resource leaves it. Import it by in-app purchase ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_territories" "all" {}

resource "apple_in_app_purchase_availability" "coins" {
  in_app_purchase_id           = apple_in_app_purchase.coins.id
  available_in_new_territories = true
  territories                  = data.apple_territories.all.ids
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `available_in_new_territories` (Boolean) Whether the purchase becomes available in territories the App Store adds later.
- `in_app_purchase_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the in-app purchase, e.g. `apple_in_app_purchase.example.id`.
- `territories` (Set of String) Territories where the purchase is sold, e.g. `USA`; see `data.apple_territories`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the availability.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apple_in_app_purchase_availability.coins
  identity = {
    in_app_purchase_id = "6446452615"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `in_app_purchase_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the in-app purchase.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apple_in_app_purchase_availability.coins 6446452615
```
